summary:
Your volume has been remarkably stable — 127 km over the last four weeks against 125 km in the prior four, with run count identical at nine each. That's not stagnation; it reflects a sustained aerobic base being held rather than built, which is appropriate context given the 44 km effort on June 8 anchoring the recent period. The current streak matching your all-time best at 20 weeks consecutive is worth noting as a structural indicator of consistency, not just a number.

Today's 13.77 km at 5:48 /km with HR 137 sits at the easy end of your range and pairs naturally with Monday's similar 11.73 km at 5:59 /km — two low-load aerobic efforts bookending what was a moderate week after last Saturday's tempo-quality 15.73 km at 4:49 /km (HR 161, load 239). That June 27 session is the standout of the recent block: the pace is ~25 seconds/km faster than your recent easy efforts, HR consistent with threshold-adjacent work, and the load more than double any other session this week. It's a meaningful quality touch in an otherwise aerobic-dominant week.

Your lactate threshold logged today at 4:24 /km @ 178 bpm is a solid anchor — it sits between your 10K PB pace (4:12) and half marathon PB pace (4:18), which is physiologically coherent for a threshold marker and suggests your speed end hasn't degraded despite the predominantly moderate volume of recent weeks. With only today's reading in the 30-day window, treat the number as a baseline being established rather than a trend, but there's no red flag in the value itself.
